'''Miguel Angel Fernández Sanjuán''' (Miguel A. F. Sanjuán) is a Spanish Theoretical Physicist from [[Leon, Spain]]. He is known for his contributions in [[nonlinear dynamics]], [[chaos theory]], and [[control of chaos]],<ref>{{citation|title=Un simple atasco es un buen ejemplo de la Teoría del Caos|url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/revista/un-simple-atasco-es-un-buen-ejemplo-de-teoria-del-caos-_421841.html|journal=Diario de León|date=December 7, 2008}}.</ref> and has published several scientific papers and popular news articles. He has supervised around 20 PhD students in Nonlinear Dynamics, Chaos and Complex Systems.

==Career==
He was a professor at the University of Valladolid during the 1982–1984 period and later he became a professor at the Polytechnic University of Madrid, 1986–1997.
Currently Miguel A. F. Sanjuán is a professor of physics at [[Rey Juan Carlos University]] in [[Madrid, Spain]].<ref>{{citation|title=  Information from Spanish Royal Society of Physics  |url=http://www.rsef2.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=251%3Acandidatura-a-la-junta-de-gobierno-de-la-rsef-miguel-angel-fernandez-sanjuan&catid=69&Itemid=137}}</ref>
He is also the director of the department of physics and the director of the Research Group on Nonlinear Dynamics, Chaos Theory and Complex Systems. 
He had coauthored several scientific articles with [[Celso Grebogi]], [[Edward Ott]], [[James A. Yorke]], [[Ying-Cheng Lai]] and Lock Yue Chew etc. 
Prof. Miguel AF Sanjuán acted as Faculty Sponsor of the Doctorate Honoris Causa granted to [[James A. Yorke|Prof. James A. Yorke]] by the [[King Juan Carlos University|Universidad Rey Juan Carlos]] in Madrid, Spain, on January 28, 2014.<ref>{{citation |title= James Yorke investido doctor 'honoris causa' por la URJC |url= http://www.ucci.urjc.es/james-yorke-investido-doctor-honoris-causa-por-la-urjc/ |access-date= 2015-06-18 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180615215851/http://www.ucci.urjc.es/james-yorke-investido-doctor-honoris-causa-por-la-urjc/ |archive-date= 2018-06-15 |url-status= dead }}</ref>
[[File:Yorke and Miguel.jpg|thumb|260px| [[James A. Yorke|Prof. James A. Yorke]]  and Prof. Miguel A. F. Sanjuán on the occasion of the Honorary doctorates ceremony at Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (2014).]]

==Awards==
He is a foreign member of [[Lithuanian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|title=  Foreign members of Lithuanian Academy of Sciences|url=http://lma.lt/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&layout=item&id=366&Itemid=230&lang=en}}</ref> In 2017, he was elected as ordinary member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{citation|title= Members of the Academy of Europe |url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Sanjuan_Miguel_Angel}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=El profesor Miguel Ángel Fernández Sanjuán, elegido miembro ordinario de la Academia Europaea |url=https://www.urjc.es/nombres-propios/2652-el-profesor-miguel-angel-fernandez-sanjuan-elegido-miembro-ordinario-de-la-academia-europaea }}</ref>

On the year 2002, he has secured the fellowship of the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science. He has also worked as a visiting researcher in many countries, including Germany, Lithuania, Italy, the United States, Japan, Portugal, India, China. On the year 2015, Prof. Miguel A. F. Sanjuan became the elected member of [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]] ([[Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales|Real Academia de Ciencias]]).<ref>{{citation|title=EL PROFESOR MIGUEL ÁNGEL FERNÁNDEZ SANJUÁN, NUEVO ACADÉMICO CORRESPONDIENTE DE LA REAL ACADEMIA DE CIENCIAS|url=http://www.urjc.es/actualidad/noticias/1243-el-profesor-miguel-angel-fernandez-sanjuan-nuevo-academico-correspondiente-de-la-real-academia-de-ciencias}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Académicos, Ilmo. Sr. D. MIGUEL ÁNGEL FERNÁNDEZ SANJUÁN|url=http://www.rac.es/2/2_ficha.php?id=974&idN3=6&idN4=50}}</ref>  Prof. Miguel Angel Fernandez Sanjuan has received one of the Research Excellence Awards in the category of Sciences granted by the Social Council of the Rey Juan Carlos University in 2016.<ref>{{citation|title=Research Excellence Awards granted by the Social Council of the Universidad Rey Juan Carlos URJC in 2016.|url=http://urjc.es/todas-las-noticias-de-actualidad-cientifica/1750-premios-cei-2015-y-del-consejo-social-a-la-excelencia-investigadora}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences twitter announcement |url=https://twitter.com/RACiencias/status/692654178347413504}}</ref> In 2017 he has been Fulbright Visiting Research Scholar at the Institute of Physical Science and Technology of the University of Maryland at College Park.

==Writings==
Together with [[Celso Grebogi]] (University of Aberdeen, UK) he was the editor of the book "Recent Progress In Controlling Chaos".<ref>{{citation|title=Recent Progress In Controlling Chaos|url=http://www.worldscibooks.com/chaos/7563.html|bibcode=2010rpcc.book.....S|year=2010|last1=Sanjuan|first1=Miguel A. F.|display-authors=etal|access-date=2011-09-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406234124/http://www.worldscibooks.com/chaos/7563.html|archive-date=2012-04-06|url-status=dead}}</ref>
On 2017 he has acted as the editor of the book titled ''Chaotic, Fractional, and Complex Dynamics'', along with Mark Edelman and Elbert Macau.<ref>{{citation|title=Chaotic, Fractional, and Complex Dynamics: New Insights and Perspectives|url=https://www.springer.com/us/book/9783319681085|isbn=9783319681085|publisher=Springer|year=2018|series=Understanding Complex Systems}}</ref>

He has authored a book in Spanish titled ''Las Matemáticas y la Física del Caos''<ref>{{citation|title=Las Matemáticas y la Física del Caos|url=http://www.madrimasd.org/blogs/complejidad/2010/01/17/131405 }}</ref> (Mathematics and Physics of Chaos), which is co-authored by Manuel de Leon of the Institute of Mathematical Sciences, CSIC.<ref>{{citation|title=CSIC|url=http://www.csic.es}}</ref> His  active  Spanish blog is greatly helping common public to improve the basic understanding of chaos theory and complexity. He has also written some popular articles in Spanish newspapers.<ref>{{citation|title=El caos no es lo que parece|url=http://www.madrimasd.org/queesmadrimasd/en_prensa/dossier/dossierdesglose.asp?id=307|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120815001150/http://www.madrimasd.org/queesmadrimasd/en_prensa/dossier/dossierdesglose.asp?id=307|archivedate=2012-08-15}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Comunicar la ciencia es un deber social|url=http://www.oei.es/divulgacioncientifica/entrevistas_222.htm}}</ref> On the year 2016, Prof. S. Rajasekar  and Prof. Miguel A. F. Sanjuan have published a book on [[Nonlinear resonance|Nonlinear Resonances]].<ref>{{citation|title=Nonlinear Resonances, Series: Springer series in synergetics|url=https://www.springer.com/fr/book/9783319248844|isbn=9783319248844|publisher=Springer|year=2016|series=Springer Series in Synergetics}}</ref> He has also co-authored a book named ''Predictability of Chaotic Dynamics'', which is primarily concerned with the computational aspects of predictability of dynamical systems.<ref>{{citation|title=Predictability of Chaotic Dynamics|url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783319518923|isbn=9783319847719|publisher=Springer|year=2017|series=Springer Series in Synergetics}}</ref>

==Research==
He and his co-authors ([[Judy Kennedy]], [[Edward Ott]] and [[James A. Yorke]]) have explored a temporally periodic flow with a time varying perturbation.  In this flow, they showed the presence of  indecomposable continua associated to the chaotic dynamics of the fluids.<ref>{{citation|title=Indecomposable Continua and the Characterization of Strange Sets in Nonlinear Dynamics, Phys. Rev. Lett. 78, 1892–1895 (1997).|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.78.1892}}</ref> He was the first to prove numerically  the [[Lakes of Wada|Wada properties]] of the exit basins of  an open Hamiltonian system.<ref>{{citation|title=Wada basins and chaotic invariant sets in the Hénon-Heiles system, Phys. Rev. E 64, 066208 (2001) |url=http://pre.aps.org/abstract/PRE/v64/i6/e066208 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140218183235/http://pre.aps.org/abstract/PRE/v64/i6/e066208 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2014-02-18 }}</ref>
